title: 1983 AHSME Problem 24

concepts.label: Power scaling of length, area, and volume

statement: How many non-congruent right triangles are there such that the perimeter in cm and area in \(\text{cm}^2\) are numerically equal?

solutions.text:
Start with any right triangle having perimeter \(P\) and area \(K.\) Scaling every side by \(k=\frac{P}{K}\) produces perimeter \(kP\) and area \(k^2K,\) which are equal. Infinitely many nonsimilar right-triangle shapes exist, and the resulting triangles are therefore noncongruent.

Therefore, the correct answer is E.
hints: Start with any shape of right triangle and scale all its side lengths by \(k\)
Under scaling, perimeter is multiplied by \(k\) while area is multiplied by \(k^2\)
